ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: MANDATORY: (a) screening of all UBOs, proposed legal representatives, directors and shareholders against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (b) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; (c) Vietnamese domestic anti-terrorism and blacklist databases maintained by the Ministry of Public Security; (d) domestic PEP identification using the State Bank of Vietnam AML guidance under Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN; (e) adverse media and worldwide regulatory enforcement screening; (f) affirmation of the entire beneficial ownership chain through a statutory UBO declaration submitted with the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate dossier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng Thông Tin Quốc Gia Về Đăng Ký Doanh Nghiệp) at https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn, administered by the Business Registration Administration under the Ministry of Planning and Investment, with offline submission at the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in the Vietnamese alphabet. A full legal name must consist of the company type designation 'Công ty TNHH' or 'Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn' followed by a proper name in Vietnamese. Foreign-language words may be transliterated phonetically into Vietnamese script; foreign original names may only be used as an auxiliary or abbreviated name. Names may include Arabic numerals, uppercase and lowercase Vietnamese letters, the symbol '.' and the ampersand '&' only. Names identical or confusingly similar to any previously registered enterprise in the Vietnamese national registration database are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Thành phố (City designation requiring administrative approval)
Bộ Công an (Ministry of Public Security)
Ngân hàng Nhà nước (State Bank of Vietnam)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a first-instance administrative complaint with the Director of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment under the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13 within 90 days from receipt of the rejection notification. The DPI must resolve the complaint within 30 to 45 days. If unsatisfied, the applicant may appeal to the Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee or institute an administrative lawsuit before the competent provincial Administrative Court within 30 days of receiving the appellate decision. In parallel, the applicant may immediately propose a revised alternative company name through the National Business Registration Portal to avoid operational delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Low acceptance for this industry. An on-site factory pre-shipment inspection and testing agency in Viet Nam must maintain a physical, lease-backed registered office in an appropriate commercial property. A pure virtual office or PO Box address will not satisfy the Enterprise Registration Certificate requirements or the licensing conditions of the Ministry of Industry and Trade / competent inspection regulatory authority. The lease agreement must cover the full corporate term or be renewable, and the proposed legal representative must be verifiable at the registered address. Certain DPI offices require evidence of lawful use of the premises and may reject short-term sublease or home-office addresses for licensed technical inspection activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% to 55% quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of registration by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment, tax authorities, or inspection-licensing authorities. The risk materially increases to approximately 70% where the Investment Registration Certificate route requires inter-agency consultation due to the technical inspection and quality-control licensing scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (enterprise establishment and registration, LLC governance, capital contribution, legal representative and registered office provisions); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 (foreign investment project registration and Investment Registration Certificate); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP (business registration procedures and dossier requirements); Law on Product and Goods Quality No. 05/2023/QH15 and Decree No. 107/2016/ND-CP (industry conformity assessment licensing, applicable to inspection bodies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) where the head office is located; for projects in industrial parks and export processing zones, the Management Board of the Industrial Park/EPZ/Economic Zone; central coordination by the Agency for Business Registration of the Ministry of Planning and Investment through the National Business Registration Portal (dkdn.gov.vn).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) with the Company Charter and ancillary forms under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP; official instrument of result: Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký doanh nghiệp).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum charter capital is imposed by the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 for an LLC engaged in ISIC 7120 (commercial inspection, testing and QC services). The members determine the charter capital freely; each member must contribute its subscribed capital in full within 90 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate date. No escrow account is mandated by law for this sector; capital may be contributed by remitting lawful Vietnamese dong or permitted foreign exchange to the company's capital contribution account at a licensed bank in Vietnam, with bank credit advices retained as contribution evidence. Foreign investors must ensure the charter capital is consistent with the total investment capital stated in the Investment Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025/FTG OF THE MEMBERS' COUNCIL (OR OWNER) OF [FULL COMPANY NAME] LTD.

ADOPTED in writing on [DAY] [MONTH] 2025 by unanimous written consent of all members holding 100% of the charter capital, without holding a meeting, in accordance with the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and the Company Charter.

WHEREAS: (A) The Company, a foreign-invested limited liability company, is being formed under the laws of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to carry on on-site factory pre-shipment quality inspection, product quality control, testing and audit services within ISIC 7120 / NAICS 541380; (B) The Company intends to apply for the Investment Registration Certificate, the Enterprise Registration Certificate, tax registration and the industry conformity assessment registration.

IT IS UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVED THAT:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The charter capital of the Company is fixed at VND [AMOUNT], approximately USD [EQUIVALENT], subscribed by the members in the proportions stated in the Company Charter. The Legal Representative shall open the Company's capital contribution account at a licensed commercial bank in Vietnam and procure that each member contributes its subscribed amount in full within 90 days from the Enterprise Registration Certificate date. The Company acknowledges that no escrow account is legally required for the inspection/QC sector; contribution evidence shall comprise bank credit advices and payment instructions.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office and head office of the Company shall be fixed at [FULL ADDRESS, PROVINCE/CITY], Vietnam, where the corporate seal, statutory books and accounting records will be kept.
3. ADOPTION OF CHARTER. The Company Charter submitted with the enterprise registration dossier is approved and adopted as the constitutional instrument of the Company.
4. APPOINTMENTS. [NAME] is appointed Legal Representative under Article 12 of the Law on Enterprises; [NAME] is appointed Chairman of the Members' Council (or President of the Company, for a single-member LLC); and [NAME] is appointed General Director with day-to-day management authority. Each appointee shall serve until written revocation.
5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Legal Representative and General Director are jointly and severally directed and authorized to: (i) sign, file and correct the enterprise registration, investment registration, tax, seal and conformity assessment dossiers; (ii) obtain the company seal and notify a specimen seal on the National Business Registration Portal; (iii) open bank accounts, sign contracts, issue invoices and receipts; (iv) execute all ancillary instruments as required by competent authorities; and (v) act as the sole signatory for corporate filings.
6. GOVERNANCE. The financial year of the Company shall coincide with the calendar year; accounting shall be kept in Vietnamese dong under the Vietnamese Accounting Regime; the Company will adopt internal segregation-of-duties, anti-money-laundering-screening for client engagements (low inherent risk tier), and quality-assurance procedures compliant with ISO/IEC 17020 before the first inspection assignment is accepted.

CERTIFIED as the unanimous act of the Members' Council (or Owner), this [DAY] day of [MONTH] 2025.

Signed: ______________________ (Chairman of the Members' Council / Owner)
Signed: ______________________ (Member / Secretary)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) of the Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam; national e-tax portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; National Business Registration Portal: https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; provincial/city Tax Departments exercise delegated local administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) where the foreign-invested project requires investment approval (or file an investment registration dossier for sectoral/conditional business lines). Step 2: File the enterprise registration dossier with the provincial Business Registration Office (Phòng Đăng ký kinh doanh) in the form of a Limited Liability Company (single-member or multi-member); the dossier is filed online at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn. Step 3: Upon issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký doanh nghiệp), the Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế) is statutorily issued simultaneously and printed on the ERC; no separate TIN application is required. Step 4: Access the e-tax portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) using a licensed digital signature (chữ ký số) and CA-issued certificate, authenticate the tax account, and file the tax department information declaration (mẫu TK-ĐKKD/ĐTNTT). Step 5: Register the e-invoice template (mẫu hóa đơn điện tử) and the designated VAT e-invoice issuing with the General Department of Taxation, and register the company's bank accounts. Step 6: Apply for activation of the 10-digit customs identification code with the General Department of Customs (VNACCS/VCIS) if the company will export goods or supply goods/imports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. The LLC is mandatorily classified as a corporate income tax (CIT) taxpayer on its worldwide income (standard CIT 20%); 100% pass-through is not available. Statutory election/relief mechanisms: (i) foreign tax credit election for foreign-source income of resident enterprises under Circular 78/2013/TT-BTC, capped at the Vietnamese CIT payable on the same net foreign-source income; (ii) election to carry forward tax losses for up to 5 consecutive years (no carryback); (iii) request for CIT incentives only if the scope meets investment/sectoral incentive conditions (e.g., high-tech, supporting industry, new investment in eligible industrial zones); (iv) transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation election (Full Local File / Master File) under Decree 132/2020/NĐ-CP; (v) no domestic hybrid mismatch or partnership-classification election is recognized; MLI-consistent GAAR (Decree 132/2020) overrides artificial arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Thuế Giá Trị Gia Tăng)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold triggers registration for a juridical entity: a foreign-invested LLC must register for VAT and issue e-invoices immediately upon incorporation and before any revenue activity. A household/individual business becomes VAT-registrable when annual revenue meets or exceeds VND 100,000,000; below that threshold it may register voluntarily. Any foreign contractor with a PE or carrying on activities in Vietnam is likewise required to register (or apply the Foreign Contractor Withholding mechanism).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vietnam has a mandatory national e-invoicing regime (Law on Tax Administration 38/2019, Decree 123/2020/NĐ-CP, Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC). All VAT invoices must be electronic XML invoices with a machine-readable QR code, issued through the eTax e-invoice service. Two modes: (1) e-invoices with tax-authority codes are cleared in real time: the tax authority's system digitally stamps each invoice before issuance; this mode is compulsory for taxpayers that fail technical/IT compliance conditions; and (2) e-invoices without pre-codes (for compliant taxpayers) must have their full XML data uploaded/transmitted to the General Department of Taxation's e-invoice data portal on a per-issuance basis within the statutory deadline (generally no later than the end of the next working day; the eTax portal supports M2M/API transmission). There is no per-invoice approval for mode (2). Digital stamping is evidenced by the tax authority's 'mã của cơ quan thuế' and the e-invoice QR code; non-compliant paper/CSV invoices are legally invalid for input VAT input credit and customs clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies only where goods are physically exported from Vietnam and supported by an export sales contract, customs export declaration (VNACCS/VCIS), bill of lading/airway bill and non-cash payment in convertible currency received at a licensed bank. Services: 0% applies only to services rendered to foreign organizations/individuals and consumed entirely outside Vietnam, and to certain services directly related to export goods (e.g., international transport of goods and related loading/transit/dispatch services). A factory inspection, QC testing, or pre-shipment audit service performed by a Vietnamese LLC is treated as consumed in Vietnam unless the taxpayer can show that the service is performed for the account of a foreign principal, the inspection is a contractual condition of the export sale of the inspected goods, and the goods (or the service output) cross the Vietnamese border; the tax authority will deny 0% where the inspection report is delivered to the foreign buyer but the actual testing/audit activity occurs entirely in Vietnam - in that case VAT at 10% (or 8% for qualifying temporary-reduction supplies) must be charged. Zero-rating evidence includes the contract, foreign client certification, export customs declaration, inspection report, and bank receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Tờ khai hải quan xuất khẩu) in VNACCS/VCIS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
VAT electronic invoice for the export sale
Proof of non-cash foreign exchange settlement (SWIFT/bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds) - e.g., Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank statement
Certificate of Origin (where requested by importer/for preferential treatment)
Service completion certificate / inspection report and certificate of foreign consumption for exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for improper zero-rating/export fraud: (i) reversal of 0% and imposition of 10% VAT on the under-collected sales, plus late-payment interest at 0.03%/day on under-remitted VAT; (ii) administrative penalties under Decree 125/2020/NĐ-CP - fines up to 3 times the evaded amount for tax evasion and additional fines for invoice violations (paper fake invoices, undeclared invoices), typically VND 10-50 million per e-invoice violation; (iii) customs/foreign-exchange scrutiny: failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days (or 360-720 days with State Bank approval) is punishable under Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN, with possible administrative sanctions for foreign-exchange violations and denial of future export zero-rating; (iv) criminal liability under Penal Code Article 200 where evaded tax exceeds VND 100 million - with evasion from VND 300 million or distinctive aggravating features leading to fines up to VND 15 billion, suspension of operation and imprisonment of up to 20 years for individuals; (v) retrospective re-assessment period is 5 years (or 10 years where fraud/omission is established) with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV / Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam). Foreign-exchange administration is exercised through the SBV Foreign Exchange Department under the Foreign Exchange Ordinance No. 06/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, Decree No. 70/2014/ND-CP, and SBV Circular No. 05/2014/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular No. 01/2019/TT-NHNN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese dong (VND) is not fully convertible. Current-account convertibility is available for the commercial inspection/testing/QC company's service-export fees, commissions, and ordinary operating disbursements, which may be converted through authorized credit institutions against underlying contract documentation. The capital account remains conditional: equity injections, shareholder loans, divestments, and profit remittances must follow the licensed Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), be routed through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at a licensed bank, and must clear tax, audit, and SBV foreign-exchange reporting gates. Profit remittance is permitted annually after audited financial statements show distributable after-tax retained earnings and after full corporate income tax settlement; no additional dividend-remittance withholding is imposed on the foreign shareholder of a Vietnamese LLC, but the remitting LLC must submit to the bank the profit-allocation resolution, audited statements, tax finalization proof, and the SBV-required documentation package.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service-export proceeds (inspection and QC fees invoiced by the LLC to offshore principals) are current-account receipts and must be repatriated directly to an authorized bank account. Under SBV Circular No. 05/2014/TT-NHNN, export earnings may be credited to and retained in the LLC's foreign-currency account, with the bank applying a 90-day repatriation monitoring window measured from the contractual payment due date unless the underlying contract expressly provides a longer payment term. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary service exporters: up to 100% of foreign-currency export proceeds may be retained on account or sold to the servicing bank at the SBV-listed rate. Mandatory conversion/surrender obligations apply only to specified state-regulated goods (e.g., crude oil) under annual SBV directives and therefore do not affect the commercial inspection LLC. Proceeds may not be parked in non-bank digital wallets, crypto corridors, or offshore EMI accounts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability. Foreign digital EMI/neo-bank rails (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business-class wallets, and comparable offshore accounts) are not recognized in Viet Nam as licensed banking accounts and cannot be used as the primary cross-border clearing rail for an FDI LLC. They fail the mandatory SBV reporting rails, cannot evidence export-proceeds repatriation, cannot serve as a Direct Investment Capital Account, and create AML misclassification risk. They may operate only as an ancillary convenience for de minimis client refunds in foreign jurisdictions where a principal insists on the rail, but the statutory books and SBV surveillance must treat the licensed Vietnamese bank account as the exclusive repository of export proceeds and investment capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial corporate onboarding of a 100% foreign-invested LLC in Viet Nam. The legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner, or a specially appointed authorized signatory holding a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney, must attend an in-branch interview; the relationship manager also performs a physical verification visit to the registered business address. Fully remote corporate account opening is not permitted by the state-owned commercial banks generally; video KYC may be used for pre-screening only, while the final signature on the account-opening resolution, the FX-transaction authorization, and the DICA mandate must be wet-ink signed in-country or by the in-country authorized representative. Board meetings held offshore do not substitute for the Vietnamese presence requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote/digital-only applicant: director and beneficial owner are not physically present for interview and no local authorized signatory is appointed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter and board resolution appointing the Vietnamese legal representative/or authorized signatory; notarized and apostilled/consular-legalized power of attorney with certified Vietnamese translation; passport copies of director and beneficial owner; Certificate of Business Registration and Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) of the LLC; registered-address lease agreement with utility verification; board resolution covering opening of the DICA and settlement account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-flow mismatch: the LLC has no local operating revenue and all collections arrive in USD from foreign clients, triggering an unexplained-flows alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current master service agreements with each offshore principal appointing the LLC as on-site factory inspection, pre-shipment QC, and audit agency; invoice schedule and fee proofs; inspection/test certificates and audit deliverables; export-of-services BOP statistical worksheet filed with the bank for each transaction; audited financial statements and corporate income-tax declarations showing the service-export revenue is fully declared; bank statements of the LLC demonstrating consistent collections against the contract funnel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-address anomaly: shared virtual office or incomplete street-address record prevents verification of the physical establishment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease agreement with nameplate letterhead and landlord identification; land-use/office ownership certificate of the lessor where available; monthly utility bills and on-site photographs; notification filed with the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the exact operational address; internal operations manual evidencing calibrated testing equipment and administrative staff retained at the premises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or split-funding remittance pattern: multiple USD SWIFT credits arrive without purpose text or with recurring identical amounts inconsistent with inspection-fee economics.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction reconciliation file linking each SWIFT reference to the underlying purchase order or inspection work order; final inspection certificate and test result; invoice and tax invoice issued under Vietnamese invoice regulations; letter from the offshore principal confirming no other beneficial party; board affidavit explaining the commercial rationale for each aggregate settlement; five-year internal compliance archive of the transaction trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Attempt to route receipts through a non-bank EMI, crypto, or multi-hop corridor instead of the licensed onshore banking rail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written board-approved undertaking to use only authorized credit institutions for all cross-border flows; consolidated extracts of the restored DICA and settlement-account SWIFT records; amended remittance policy; SBV supervisory declaration confirming source of funds and remediation plan; evidence that any historical EMI usage has been wound down; tax and accounting firm AML/CFT opinion confirming future proceeds settle exclusively through the licensed Vietnamese bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Charter capital must be remitted by the foreign investor only to the LLC's Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at a licensed commercial bank, quoting the purpose 'contribution to charter capital of the foreign-invested enterprise' and the IRC registration number; the bank verifies the inflow against the IRC schedule, the charter contribution timetable, and SBV reporting codes, after which funds may be converted to VND for operating use. All export-of-services fees from offshore principals are settled by SWIFT MT103 credits to the LLC's foreign-currency or VND current account; each credit must carry the payer's name, a reference to the underlying inspection contract, an invoice, and the standard SBV balance-of-payments purpose classification for service-export receipts. No third-party, crypto, or digital-EMI corridor is acceptable for inbound funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplies, subcontractor fees, laboratory calibration, rent, and payroll are settled via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border counterparties, supported by underlying contracts, tax invoices, and withholding-tax receipts where applicable; for goods-related service components such as calibrated testing equipment or reference materials, a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection may be used if the counterparty requires bank confirmation. Domestic VND payments clear through the interbank EFA system and NAPAS. Because inspection/QC service exports do not move goods, transport documents are not required; the LC route is limited to tangible-equipment acquisitions and back-to-back performance guarantees demanded by clients for factory-audit mandates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore VND/USD spot FX with an authorized credit institution against current-account underlying transactions
Onshore VND/USD FX forward with maximum tenor of 365 days supported by a documented current-account or debt-service exposure
Onshore VND/USD FX swap with an authorized bank for short-term liquidity bridging
Cross-currency swap linked to a registered shareholder loan or syndicated facility on a case-by-case SBV-licensed basis
Offshore VND non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as a hedging or clearing rail; all hedging must be executed through the licensed onshore banking system

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động của doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; by 31 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 5,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 for late or non-submission; repeated non-filing for one year leads to classification as an inactive enterprise and eventual administrative strike-off of the Enterprise Registration Certificate by the DPI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements submitted to the tax authority and the DPI, with certified copies retained at the head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department and Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; by 31 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to VND 15,000,000 under Decree 125/2020/NĐ-CP for failure to submit financial statements to the tax authority; non-audited submissions by a foreign-invested enterprise are invalid and expose the company to forced administrative assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax finalization dossier (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN) with balance payment due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Finalization return and balance payment within 90 days after fiscal year end; by 31 March for calendar-year companies; quarterly CIT advance declarations due by the 30th day of the following quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to VND 40,000,000 depending on delay; late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; underdeclaration penalties up to 20% of the underpaid CIT; persistent default triggers tax enforcement measures and deregistration risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business license fee (lệ phí môn bài) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by 30 January of each calendar year; VND 2,000,000 where charter capital is at or below VND 10 billion and VND 3,000,000 where charter capital exceeds VND 10 billion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fines up to VND 25,000,000 for non-declaration or underpayment; continued non-payment may lead to tax enforcement measures and suspension of e-invoice issuance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual personal income tax finalization return (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNCN) for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after calendar year end; by 31 March for calendar-year companies; monthly or quarterly PIT withholding returns due by the 20th or 30th day after the period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to VND 40,000,000; arrears interest at 0.03% per day; failure to withhold or remit PIT may incur penalties up to 20% of the unpaid amount.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 34 of Law on Accounting No. 88/2015/QH13 and Decree 174/2016/NĐ-CP, every foreign-invested enterprise in Vietnam must obtain an independent audit of its annual financial statements irrespective of revenue, assets, or employee count; no size threshold applies to this LLC. The audit must be performed by a firm holding a certificate of eligibility for audit services.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) under Law on Accounting No. 88/2015/QH13 and MOF circulars; IFRS may be applied voluntarily by qualifying foreign-invested enterprises under Decision 345/2020/QĐ-BTC for consolidated group reporting, while statutory standalone financial statements remain under VAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO return exists for a non-financial private LLC in Vietnam. The LLC must maintain a Register of Members under Article 82 of Law on Enterprise No. 59/2020/QH14, validly recording every capital contribution and capital transfer before rights are enforced against the company; member changes must be notified to the DPI within 10 days via the e-registration portal. The annual enterprise report, which confirms current member composition, operates as the annual confirmation; share transfers to foreign investors require the DPI to update the foreign investment registration record.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (sổ đăng ký thành viên)
Book of minutes and resolutions of Members' Meetings and Management Board
Register and appointment records of the General Director and supervisory personnel

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 to US$1,200 per year for registered address, mail handling, and corporate secretarial agency services in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City; larger compliance outsourcing packages US$1,500 to US$3,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,000 to US$5,000 for an SME foreign-invested services LLC using a mid-tier licensed audit firm; US$6,000 to US$10,000 if a Big Four firm is retained.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SMEs with total annual revenue not exceeding VND 3 billion are subject to 15%; enterprises in qualified high-tech, supporting industry, or incentivized sector/investment locations may enjoy 10% for 15 years, tax holidays (4-year exemption and 9-year 50% reduction), and other preferential rates as prescribed by Vietnam's CIT Law; foreign-invested quality control and testing companies operating as independent service providers generally apply the standard 20% rate unless eligible for investment incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax finalization return Form 03/TNDN; provisional quarterly payments via Form 02/TNDN or the integrated e-tax declaration system; submitted electronically through the General Department of Taxation's National Public Service Portal / eTax (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Provisional quarterly CIT payments due by the 30th day of the first month of the following quarter; annual finalization return due within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year (generally by March 31 if the fiscal year ends on December 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A – Enterprise identification (name, tax code, address)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, enterprise tax identification number, registered address, and contact details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foreign investor must ensure the Vietnamese branch/LLC's tax code is used; foreign parent details, if any, are provided in Schedule of related-party transactions rather than as the taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Period of tax finalization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory Vietnamese fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) unless an approved different accounting year has been registered

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 – Revenue from sales and services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross turnover from factory inspection, testing, quality control, and audit agency services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Vietnam-source service revenue; if services are rendered to overseas clients for overseas goods, analyze PE exposure and apply Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) nexus rules carefully

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of services, employee salaries, subcontractor costs, travel, depreciation, and administrative expenses actually incurred and supported by lawful invoices/vouchers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility rules apply equally; expenses paid to related parties must satisfy arm's length conditions for deduction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains, and other incidental income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Statement of foreign-source income and applicable foreign tax credit claims, if any

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses offset against current-year taxable income, maximum carryforward 5 years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from Vietnamese operations of the Vietnamese entity can be carried forward; foreign losses are not recognized

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory CIT rate or preferential rate, with legal basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify eligibility for supporting industry or high-tech service incentives; otherwise apply 20%

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 – CIT payable / amount already provisionally paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated tax and quarterly provisional payments already made, netting to remaining payable or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underpayment of 20% or more against finalization is subject to interest; reconcile carefully before submission

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule – Related-party transactions (Form 03-7/TNDN or GCN related-party disclosure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions, transfer pricing methodologies, and arm's length range
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent/affiliate service fees, management fees, royalties, and intercompany loan terms must be disclosed plus Local File if threshold met

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 10-15% of tax arrears (or 20-30% if tax evasion intent) plus late payment interest at 0.03%/day on unpaid amounts; administrative fines for late submission of returns and related documents can reach VND 15-25 million for serious delays, and failure to finalize within 90 days is treated as non-filing and may trigger enforced collection, tax assessment, and suspended invoices.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends distributed by a Vietnamese LLC/company to its foreign corporate shareholder (corporate income tax is the sole entity-level tax; no separate dividend withholding tax for foreign corporate investors under Vietnam's domestic CIT law)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although Vietnam generally does not impose dividend WHT on corporate shareholders, foreign investors relying on a DTA for reduced rates or to claim treaty protection must submit: (1) a withholding tax exemption/reduction dossier to the Vietnamese tax authority, (2) a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction's competent authority, (3) a declaration of beneficial ownership, and (4) supporting documents evidencing no permanent establishment in Vietnam. The tax authority reviews and issues a written confirmation before any treaty-relief application is honored; the DTA application form is typically submitted before or with the tax finalization return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 10% WHT under domestic law (and foreign contractor tax provisions may apply at a combined rate on gross consideration, generally 10% CIT on deemed income basis plus 5% VAT-like FCT, though pure royalty arrangements are subject to royalty WHT rules, depending on the contract characterization). Interest paid to non-residents generally 5% WHT. Under common Vietnamese DTAs, royalty rates are often reduced to 5-10% (e.g., 10% under many treaties, 7.5% or 5% under specific agreements) and interest rates to 5-10% (typically 10%); treaty relief requires the same TRC/beneficial ownership protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 50 billion (approximately US$2 million) of related-party revenue in a fiscal year; also lower thresholds for related-party transactions with exemptions: small taxpayers with below VND 50 billion revenue and related-party transactions below VND 30 billion may be exempt from certain documentation, but the related-party transaction disclosure form must still be filed if the enterprise has related-party transactions exceeding VND 30 billion, subject to detailed thresholds under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam applies the substance-over-form doctrine and requires related-party transactions to reflect economic substance; although Vietnam does not have 'Economic Substance Regulations' identical to the UAE-style ESR, the domestic TP regime (Decree 132/2020/ND-CP) and CIT law deny deduction for transactions lacking commercial substance or conducted with shell entities; the General Department of Taxation can recharacterize, adjust pricing, impose deemed income, and apply penalties. The foreign contractor tax and permanent establishment rules further require substantive Vietnam presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating deductible expenses via fake invoices, understating service revenue from overseas clients, maintaining parallel accounting books, or destroying records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under Vietnam's Tax Administration Law and Penal Code: criminal liability for tax evasion (imprisonment up to 20 years in aggravated cases); administrative fines of 1-3 times the evaded tax amount; late-payment interest at 0.03%/day; forced collection and suspension of business operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/legal representatives are personally liable for filing and payment failures; the corporate veil can be pierced in fraud or intentional evasion cases, exposing personal assets for restitution; travel bans, exit visa denials, and imprisonment of directors and signatories are available enforcement measures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Vietnamese inspection/testing LLC that performs little or no actual on-site activity, outsourcing all substance to foreign affiliates, or using the entity solely for invoicing and profit parking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment, disallowance of intercompany payments, deemed CIT and foreign contractor tax assessments, fines of up to 3 times tax arrears, and cancellation/disqualification of enterprise registration under the Enterprise Law and Investment Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution for tax debts if they knowingly operated a sham entity; a court may pierce the veil where the LLC is a mere instrumentality, and legal representatives can be banned from establishing new enterprises and may face criminal prosecution for fraudulent bankruptcy or tax evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Trade or Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments via opaque channels, structuring transactions to avoid reporting, invoicing for fake inspections, or moving funds through Wise in coordination with tax misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering Law (effective 2022-2023): administrative fines up to VND 2 billion for non-compliant organizations; criminal money laundering penalties including imprisonment up to 15 years; freezing of accounts and confiscation of proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The State Bank of Vietnam and investigating police may impose personal monetary penalties on compliance officers and directors for AML failures; willful involvement attracts criminal liability, travel restrictions, and extradition exposure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the related-party transaction disclosure, not preparing Local File/Master File on time, or applying non-arm's length fees for management charges, testing protocols, or group services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP audit adjustments with additional CIT, late-payment interest, and fines up to 3 times the under-declared tax; penalties for failure to provide documentation equal to 50% of the determined tax adjustment (or 100% in bad faith); administrative fines on enterprises up to VND 20-30 million for documentation failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and accountants who sign false TP documentation can be held personally liable for administrative fines; serious willful falsification triggers criminal tax evasion liability; tax authorities may recover debts from personal bank accounts and initiate criminal complaints against legal representatives

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Business Operation / Unlawful Provision of Inspection Services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a commercial inspection, testing, and quality control agency without a statutory license, branch registration, or foreign-invested enterprise approval in Vietnam
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties for illegal business activities: fines up to VND 100 million or more depending on sector; forced suspension of operations; cancellation of tax code; the tax authorities may compute CIT on a deemed basis, and contracts may be void
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The enterprise's legal representative is subject to fines and may be prohibited from acting as legal representative; if the unlicensed operation caused significant tax or investment law violations, criminal prosecution for illegal business activities is possible
